answer: When an agent joins, its sponsor pins a claim to a growth-ring ledger and posts a cedar-wood collateral bond that a randomly drawn peer panel must audit within seventy-two hours, checking the signed interaction graph for reused addresses. Each identity is a vertex in that graph, so a clone shares edges with its parent; tracing any abuse burns collateral along the whole path and shales off a further 10% to fund the audit pool. One honest agent stakes one refundable bond, while a thousand clones need a thousand locked bonds plus log forgery that any single inconsistency collapses.
